title: canon@1 — evidence identity rules
description: Not a message shape: the machine-readable specification of how a tabular result is encoded before hashing, so that `logical_result_hash` means the same thing in both trees. A document conforming to this schema DESCRIBES a canonicalization version; the rules themselves are the `const` values below, which is what makes a drift in either implementation a test failure rather than a discussion.

logical_types.description: The closed set of column types. A source type that does not map to exactly one of these refuses sealing rather than being coerced.

scalar_encoding.description: One canonical text form per type. Every value becomes a UTF-8 byte string before hashing; NULL is distinct from every value, including the empty string.

null.const: the single byte 0x00, which no encoded value may contain

int64.const: base-10, optional leading '-', no leading zeros, no '+'

decimal.const: base-10 at the column's DECLARED scale, always with that many fraction digits, optional leading '-', no exponent, no thousands separators. 1.5 at scale 2 is '1.50'; -0 is '0.00'.

float64.const: shortest round-trip form (Rust's Display / Ryu); 'NaN', 'inf', '-inf' spelled exactly so

string.const: the UTF-8 bytes, unchanged: no case folding, no Unicode normalization, no trimming

timestamp_tz.const: RFC 3339 in UTC with 'Z' and exactly 6 fraction digits; the source offset, when known, travels in the column metadata and NOT in the value

interval.const: ISO-8601 duration, months and seconds normalized separately (P1M is not P30D)

array.const: '[' + elements in order, each encoded by its element type, separated by 0x1F + ']'

ordering.description: A result must declare how its rows are identified, or it cannot be sealed. This is the rule that stops a row-order permutation from silently changing an answer's evidence.

const: keys: the contract declares result key columns; row_id is the encoded key tuple and the result hashes as a MULTISET (row order does not matter)
position: the contract declares a TOTAL orderBy; row_id is the 0-based position and the result hashes as a SEQUENCE

refuse_when.const: neither keys nor a total orderBy is declared — the refusal code is 'result_not_identifiable'

separators.description: Field separator 0x1F, row separator 0x1E, section separator 0x1D — bytes that cannot appear in any encoded scalar.

logical_result_hash.const: sha256 over: canon version, then the schema section (each column: id, name, type, scale, unit, nullable, key flag), then the identity section (row_id rule, order_by list), then the rows. Under 'keys' the encoded rows are sorted bytewise before hashing; under 'position' they are hashed in order. Truncation status, redaction status and the authorization class are part of the identity section — a truncated result never hashes equal to the complete one.

artifact_hash.const: sha256 over the STORED BYTES (Parquet or canonical CSV) exactly as uploaded. Never conflated with the logical hash: two serializations of one logical result share a logical_result_hash and differ in artifact_hash.

identity_inputs.description: Everything that participates in logical identity. A change in any of these is a different logical result, by construction.
const: column ids, names, types, scale, unit, nullability, key flags, in order
row_id rule and the declared order_by
